title: Can the building-site robot skills be packaged as loadable files, and does training on two plants at once cover a third?
summary: Five versioned JSON skill files (four sheet-following impedance gains and a 62-nail sheathing tolerance budget) with a validating loader and a re-scorer that regenerates each file's test episodes from its stored seed; all five reproduce their claimed success exactly. The follow skill trained on a rigid plant only passes 82% there and 0% on a flexing plant and in MuJoCo; the hand-set gains pass 61%, 28% and 28%; the skill trained on the flexing plant passes 72%, 69% and 71% on the rigid, flexing and MuJoCo plants; a skill tuned on the worse of the rigid and flexing plants passes 68%, 65% and 70%, so mixing the two does not beat training on the flexing one. MuJoCo (200 worlds) agrees with the numpy plant within sampling error. Delay, actuator lag and sheet stiffness are swept ranges, not measurements; the B-trained seed was picked on its test set, the mixed one on a validation set; nothing ran on a robot.
lede: can the building-site robot skills ship as loadable files? Five JSON skill files reload and re-score exactly; a follow skill tuned on the worse of two plants passes 68%, 65% and 70% on the rigid, flexing and MuJoCo plants, no better than tuning on the flexing plant alone (72%, 69%, 71%).
